intent: Stylized in-place walking loop with the upper body maintaining a mild forward-leaning carriage through most of the cycle; the motion has pronounced lateral sway/lean, cross-steps, alternating yaw, and asymmetric arm carriage. This is not a neutral upright walk.

phases.description: Opening from a mildly forward-leaning upper-body posture: the body sways to one side, one leg opens outward, then returns to a relatively upright/passing pose.
Cross-step and torso turn; root yaw increases to its positive maximum of +31.5° at f30 while the upper body maintains a mild forward-leaning carriage.
Reverse direction through a cross-step with the pelvis at its lowest point at f37, then open toward the opposite side with pronounced whole-body sway.
Counter-step; root yaw reaches its negative minimum of -18.1° at f52, then returns to the loop seam with f63 approximately matching f0 while retaining the mild forward-leaning upper-body character.

keyPoses.description: Pelvis X is at its minimum.
The pelvis is at its lowest point while the cross-step reverses direction.
The body leans toward the opposite side with one leg extended outward.
The step opens again and the pelvis is at a local high.

weightTransfer: The pelvis shifts laterally from its X minimum at f8 to its X maximum at f34, lowers to its minimum Z at f37, then returns toward the loop seam; the side-to-side sway accompanies the stepping rhythm. No support/planted foot or contact side is assigned.
bodyMechanics: Across the cycle, the head, neck, and chest share a mildly forward-leaning carriage, giving the walk a slightly forward-pitched character rather than an upright upper body. During f35-f41, the leg/pelvis leads the directional change: LeftUpperLeg reaches its peak per-frame angular change at f35 and the pelvis reaches its lowest point at f37; chest/shoulder rotation increases at f39-f40, and RightUpperArm reaches its peak per-frame angular change at f41. The observed coordination is lower body/pelvis initiating the change, followed by the upper body and arm, while the mild forward lean is maintained.

recommended: stylized in-place walk with mild forward upper-body lean and side-to-side sway
characterful gait that is not fully upright or neutral
notRecommendedAsPrimary: neutral straight walk with an upright upper body

notes: The upper-body forward lean is mild; the evidence supports describing it as slightly forward-leaning, but not as a pronounced hunch or deep stoop.
animation.json has no contact/force channel; no support/planted foot or contact side is inferred.
